explain.say: Every building has a natural rhythm of swaying, called its natural period. Tall buildings sway slowly and short stiff ones vibrate quickly; a rough rule is about a tenth of a second per storey.

faq.q: What is a building's natural period?
faq.a: It is the time a building takes to sway back and forth once if you push it and let go. Tall, flexible buildings have long periods of several seconds, while short, stiff ones take a fraction of a second.
asks: What is the natural frequency of a building?

faq.q: What is resonance in an earthquake?
faq.a: Resonance happens when the ground shakes at the same rhythm as a building's natural sway. Each push adds to the last, so the swaying grows much larger, like pushing a child on a swing in time.
asks: Why does a matching rhythm make shaking worse?

faq.q: Why do some buildings fall in an earthquake but not others?
faq.a: Buildings whose natural rhythm matches the ground shaking sway much harder. Construction quality, materials and the soil underneath also matter a great deal.
asks: Why do neighbouring buildings behave differently in a quake?

faq.q: Why does soft soil make earthquakes worse?
faq.a: Soft soil, like an old lake bed, can amplify shaking and make it slower and longer, which can match the rhythm of taller buildings. That is what happened in Mexico City in 1985.
asks: What happened in Mexico City in 1985?

faq.a: They estimate the ground's shaking rhythm for the site and design buildings with a different natural period, add damping to soak up energy, or use base isolation to change how the building moves.

facts: A rough rule of thumb is that a building's natural period is about 0.1 seconds per storey, so a 10-storey building sways about once a second.
In the 1985 Mexico City earthquake, soft lake-bed soil amplified slow shaking, and buildings of roughly 6 to 15 storeys were the most heavily damaged.

quiz.say: The ground at a site shakes with a rhythm of about one second. Using the rule of about 0.1 seconds per storey, which building is most at risk of resonance?
quiz.show: Ground shakes about once a second. Most at risk?
quiz.why: Ten storeys times about 0.1 seconds gives a natural period near one second, matching the ground.

wrong.1: A 1-storey house sways about ten times faster than the ground's rhythm.
wrong.2: A 60-storey tower sways about once every six seconds, much slower than the ground.
